# Image spec — every image slot on every template

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/generate-image-spec.mjs from app/src/templates/imageSlots.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Hand this to a client. Every number is a measured render size in CSS pixels at the three
viewports the pages were measured at (mobile 390, tablet 820, desktop 1440); screens draw at 2× that, which is where the minimums come from.

## What to send

| Kind | Send | Minimum | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Job photographs | **1600 × 1200 px, 4:3**, JPEG or PNG. Landscape. One subject per photo — no before/after composites (they get cut through the middle in the wide slots) | 1200 × 900 | the largest 4:3 tile renders 1094 px wide on desktop; below 1200 it is upscaled on a retina screen |
| The lead removal photo (removal-a hero) | **2000 × 1500 px or larger, 4:3**. Quiet background; the headline sits on it | 1600 × 1200 | removal-a paints it 1440 px wide behind the headline on desktop (and 1656 px tall on a tablet); the pipeline caps masters at 1600, so 1600 is the floor |
| Logo | **SVG, or a transparent PNG 512 px or more on its longest edge**. No white box baked in, no phone number in the artwork | 192 px | the header shows it at 96 px, so 192 px is the 2× floor; smaller is never upscaled and looks soft |
| Section backgrounds (optional) | 1600 × 900 px, 16:9. Texture, not detail — they sit under a heavy tint | 1200 × 675 | painted full-width (1440 px) under an 84–94% tint; the marquee strip is 1180 × 62 |

iPhone HEIC files are refused with a message; export as JPEG or PNG first. Every upload is
auto-rotated, stripped of metadata, cropped to 4:3 around the focal point you click, and
re-encoded as WebP at 400 / 800 / 1200 / 1600 px wide. The original is never published.

## How photos reach the slots

A client uploads **sets**, one per service (removal, trimming, storm, generic). A template
picks from its service's set **by position** — the first removal photo is removal-a's hero
plate, the last three are its service strip — so reordering a set re-slots the photos. A
service with no photos falls back within the client (removal → generic → storm → trimming),
never to another client's photographs and never to template artwork.

Policies: **cover** slots have a fixed box and crop the photo to fill it — the focal point
you click decides what survives the crop. **frame** slots show the whole photo in its own
shape, so a grid of them is only even when every photo is the same shape (4:3).
**contain** never crops (logos). **plate** is a decorative background under a tint.
